concepts.name: Passing a point
concepts.description: Passing a pole, signal or person means covering exactly the train's own length.

concepts.name: Crossing a platform or bridge
concepts.description: Crossing something with length: the train covers its own length plus that length.

concepts.name: Trains in opposite directions
concepts.description: Relative speed is the sum of the speeds; the distance is the sum of the lengths.

concepts.name: Trains in the same direction
concepts.description: Relative speed is the difference of the speeds; overtaking covers the sum of the lengths.

concepts.name: Units: km/hr and m/s
concepts.description: Lengths are in metres and times in seconds, but speeds arrive in km/hr. Convert with 5/18.

formulas.title: Passing a pole
formulas.prompt: A train passes a pole. What distance does it cover?
formulas.formula:
Distance = Train length
Time = Length ÷ Speed
formulas.explanation: A pole has no length, so the train only has to move its own length past it.
formulas.example:
200 m train at 20 m/s
Time = 200 ÷ 20 = 10 s
formulas.commonMistake: Adding a length that is not there.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A 120 m train runs at 15 m/s. How long does it take to pass a signal post?

formulas.title: Crossing a platform
formulas.prompt: A train completely crosses a platform. What distance does it cover?
formulas.explanation: The front reaches the platform's end after the platform's length; the rest of the train must then clear it.
formulas.example:
150 m train, 250 m platform
Distance = 400 m
formulas.applicationPrompt: A 150 m train crosses a 250 m platform at 20 m/s. How long does it take?

formulas.title: Opposite directions
formulas.prompt: Two trains approach each other. How do you find the time they take to cross?
formulas.formula:
Relative speed = S₁ + S₂
Time = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)
formulas.explanation: Each train is closing the gap on the other, so the speeds add.
formulas.example:
54 and 36 km/hr → 90 km/hr = 25 m/s
Lengths 120 m + 180 m = 300 m → 12 s
formulas.applicationPrompt: Trains of 100 m and 200 m approach at 30 m/s and 20 m/s. How long do they take to cross?

formulas.title: Same direction
formulas.prompt: A faster train overtakes a slower one. How do you find the time?
formulas.formula:
Relative speed = S₁ − S₂
Time = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ (S₁ − S₂)
formulas.explanation: The faster train gains on the slower one only by the difference in speeds.
formulas.example:
72 and 36 km/hr → 36 km/hr = 10 m/s
Lengths 100 m + 140 m = 240 m → 24 s
formulas.applicationPrompt: A 100 m train at 20 m/s overtakes a 140 m train at 10 m/s. How long does it take?

formulas.title: km/hr ↔ m/s
formulas.prompt: How do you convert km/hr into m/s?

formulas.title: Pole time and platform time
formulas.prompt: A train passes a pole in t₁ seconds and a platform of known length in t₂ seconds. What is the train's length?
formulas.formula: Train length = Platform length × t₁ ÷ (t₂ − t₁)
formulas.explanation: The extra t₂ − t₁ seconds are spent covering the platform alone, which gives the speed.
formulas.example: Pole in 10 s, 300 m platform in 25 s: 300 × 10 ÷ 15 = 200 m.
formulas.commonMistake: Dividing by t₂ instead of the difference in times.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A train crosses a signal in 8 seconds and a 180 m bridge in 20 seconds.

formulas.title: Crossing times in both directions
formulas.prompt: Two trains cross in t₁ seconds running in opposite directions and t₂ seconds in the same direction. What is the ratio of their speeds?
formulas.explanation: The same total length is covered at the sum of speeds in t₁ and at the difference in t₂.
formulas.commonMistake: Writing the ratio as t₂ : t₁.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Two trains take 12 s to cross when opposed and 60 s when one overtakes the other.

levels.title: Length Is Part of the Distance
levels.description: The one question to ask first: what distance does the train actually have to cover?

blocks.title: A train is not a point
blocks.body:
In ordinary speed problems a car is a dot. A train is long, so the distance depends on what it is passing.

Passing a pole or a person: the train covers its own length.
Crossing a platform or bridge: it covers its own length plus the platform's length.

blocks.title: The distance rule
blocks.body:
Pole / person: Distance = L
Platform / bridge: Distance = L + P
blocks.caption: Then Time = Distance ÷ Speed as always.

blocks.body: Convert first. Lengths are metres and times are seconds, so change km/hr into m/s by multiplying by 5/18.

blocks.title: Two trains: add or subtract
blocks.body: Trains in opposite directions close on each other quickly: add the speeds. Trains in the same direction only gain by the difference: subtract. In both cases the distance to clear is the sum of the two lengths.

levels.title: Trains Formulas
levels.description: Distance rules, relative speed and unit conversion.

levels.title: Missing Lengths
levels.description: Work back from crossing times to lengths.

questions.question: A 200 m long train passes a pole in 8 seconds. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Passing a pole means covering the train's own length: 200 ÷ 8 = 25 m/s.
questions.method: Distance is the train's own length; divide by time.

hints.text: A pole has no length. What distance must the train travel to pass it?
Its own length: 200 m.

questions.question: A train running at 54 km/hr passes a pole in 12 seconds. What is the length of the train, in metres?
questions.method: Convert to m/s, then length = speed × time.

hints.text: The time is in seconds, so convert the speed to m/s first.

questions.question: A 150 m long train runs at 20 m/s. How long does it take to cross a 250 m long platform?

hints.text: What total distance must the train travel to clear the platform?
Add both lengths: 400 m.

commonMistakes: Using only the train length (7.5 s) or only the platform (12.5 s).

questions.question: Two trains run towards each other at 40 km/hr and 50 km/hr. At what speed are they closing on each other?
questions.explanation: Towards each other, the speeds add: 40 + 50 = 90 km/hr.

hints.text: Each train closes part of the gap. Do the closing speeds add or subtract?

commonMistakes: Subtracting the speeds, which is for same-direction motion.

questions.question: To convert a speed from km/hr to m/s you should multiply by
questions.explanation: 1 km/hr = 1000 m per 3600 s = 5/18 m/s. A speed in m/s is a smaller number than in km/hr.

hints.text: Should the number get bigger or smaller when you go from km/hr to m/s?
Smaller — so use the fraction less than 1.

questions.question: A train takes 30 seconds to cross a 300 m platform and 20 seconds to pass a pole. What is the length of the train, in metres?
questions.explanation: The extra 10 seconds are spent covering the 300 m platform, so speed = 300 ÷ 10 = 30 m/s. Length = 30 × 20 = 600 m.
solutionSteps: Extra time for the platform = 30 − 20 = 10 s.
questions.method: The difference in times covers exactly the platform.

hints.text: Crossing the platform takes longer than passing a pole. What does the extra time correspond to?
The 300 m platform in 10 seconds gives the speed.

questions.question: Two trains of length 120 m and 180 m run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 54 km/hr and 36 km/hr. How many seconds do they take to cross each other?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 90 km/hr = 25 m/s. Distance = 120 + 180 = 300 m. Time = 300 ÷ 25 = 12 s.
questions.method: Add speeds, add lengths, convert units.

hints.text: Opposite directions: what happens to the speeds and to the lengths?
Add both, then convert 90 km/hr into m/s.

questions.question: Two trains of length 100 m and 140 m run in the same direction at 72 km/hr and 36 km/hr. How long does the faster train take to completely overtake the slower one?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 72 − 36 = 36 km/hr = 10 m/s. Distance = 100 + 140 = 240 m. Time = 24 s.

hints.text: Same direction: do the speeds add or subtract?
Total distance to clear is both lengths together.

commonMistakes: Adding the speeds (8 s) or using one length only (10 s, 14 s).

questions.question: A 150 m long train runs at 63 km/hr. In how many seconds does it pass a man walking in the same direction at 3 km/hr?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 60 km/hr = 50/3 m/s. Time = 150 ÷ (50/3) = 9 s. The man has no length, so only the train's length counts.
questions.method: A person is a point: distance = train length, speed = difference.

hints.text: Same direction, so subtract the speeds.
The man is a point, so only the train length is covered.

commonMistakes: Forgetting the man is moving and using 63 km/hr.

questions.question: A passenger sitting in a train running at 36 km/hr notices that a train coming the opposite way at 54 km/hr takes 6 seconds to pass him. What is the length of the other train?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 90 km/hr = 25 m/s. Length = 25 × 6 = 150 m.
solutionSteps: The passenger is a point, so distance = the other train's length.
questions.method: Add speeds; the observer's train length does not matter.

hints.text: Speeds add. Then convert to m/s.
Multiply the relative speed by 6 s.

questions.question: A train crosses a 200 m bridge in 25 seconds and a 350 m bridge in 40 seconds. What is the length of the train, in metres?
questions.explanation: The extra 150 m of bridge takes 15 extra seconds, so speed = 10 m/s. Crossing the first bridge covers 250 m, so the train is 250 − 200 = 50 m long.
solutionSteps: Extra bridge = 150 m in 15 s → speed = 10 m/s.
questions.method: Differences isolate the speed; then subtract the bridge.

hints.text: Compare the two crossings: what is different?
Use the extra distance and extra time for the speed.

commonMistakes: Ignoring that the train length is added in both crossings.

questions.question: A 150 m long train runs at 60 km/hr towards a second train running at 48 km/hr. They take 9 seconds to cross each other. What is the length of the second train, in metres?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 108 km/hr = 30 m/s. Total distance = 30 × 9 = 270 m. Second train = 270 − 150 = 120 m.
questions.method: Total length = relative speed × time; subtract the known length.

hints.text: Find the total distance covered while crossing.
That total is both lengths added together.

commonMistakes: Taking 270 m as the second train's length alone.

questions.question: Two trains of length 200 m and 150 m run in the same direction at 90 km/hr and 72 km/hr. How long does the faster train take to completely pass the slower one?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 18 km/hr = 5 m/s. Distance = 350 m. Time = 350 ÷ 5 = 70 s.

hints.text: Same direction: subtract the speeds.
A small relative speed means a long overtaking time.

commonMistakes: Adding the speeds (about 8 s) or using one length (30 s, 40 s).
